target: बाड़ लगाई गई ताकि बच्चे सुरक्षित रहें।
english: A fence was put up so the children stay safe.
reason: Unnatural word order — Hindi ताकि clauses follow the main clause, never front it. Same passive + ताकि point, natural order.

target: जितनी जल्दी निकलोगे, उतनी जल्दी पहुँच जाओगे।
english: The earlier you leave, the earlier you'll get there.
reason: Preachy motto ("the more you sweat, the better the result"). Same जितना…उतना correlative on an everyday situation.

target: वह अगले महीने नई नौकरी शुरू करेगा।
english: He will start a new job next month.
reason: Newspaper register (आगामी) plus a spelling error — खड़ा takes no nukta, so ख़ड़ा is wrong. Same simple future in everyday speech.

target: अगले महीने बिजली का बिल ज़्यादा आएगा।
english: The electricity bill will be higher next month.
reason: Reads like a school essay on energy policy, not something a learner will ever say. Same future tense, everyday content.

target: दरवाज़ा खटखटाकर पड़ोसी ने आवाज़ लगाई।
english: The neighbour knocked on the door and called out.
reason: Wrong collocation — one knocks (खटखटाना), one does not "ring a door latch". Same -कर conjunctive participle.

target: कमल ने बड़ी मुश्किल से यह काम पूरा किया।
english: Kamal finished this work with great difficulty.
reason: Textbook motto register ("faced the challenge with great courage"). Same ने + से-instrumental structure, ordinary content.

target: डॉक्टर ने जाँच करके दवा लिख दी।
english: The doctor examined me and prescribed medicine.
reason: Niche content — a vaidya reading a pulse is not usable language. Same ने + -कर participle, everyday clinic scene.

target: अगर हम समय पर नहीं निकलेंगे तो हमें ट्रेन नहीं मिलेगी।
english: If we don't leave on time, we won't get the train.
reason: Preachy environmental-essay sentence and overlong. Same अगर…तो conditional with future, everyday stakes.

target: मेरे पापा ने मुझे गाड़ी चलाना सिखाया।
english: My dad taught me to drive.
reason: Moralising ("taught me to be a good human being"). Same verb-ना सिखाया pattern on a concrete skill.

target: फ़र्श पर गद्दा बिछाकर हम सो गए।
english: We laid a mattress on the floor and went to sleep.
reason: Subjectless and stilted, with niche तख़्त; the English gloss is not a sentence anyone says. Same -कर participle, subject restored.

target: मीटिंग रद्द कर दी गई और सबको फ़ोन पर बता दिया गया।
english: The meeting was cancelled and everyone was informed by phone.
reason: Bureaucratic police-report register. Same double passive in everyday speech.

target: इस स्कूल में बच्चों को अंग्रेज़ी भी सिखाई जाती है।
english: English is also taught to children at this school.
reason: Pointless school-textbook trivia about square roots. Same habitual passive (सिखाया जाता है), usable content.

target: गहरी साँस लेकर थोड़ी देर आराम करो।
english: Take a deep breath and rest for a while.
reason: Unnatural — नथुनों (nostrils) is clinical vocabulary no one uses in this instruction. Same -कर participle + imperative.

target: घर की दीवारें रंगी गईं और खिड़कियाँ साफ़ की गईं।
english: The house walls were painted and the windows were cleaned.
reason: Government press-release register about civic works. Same coordinated feminine-plural passives, domestic context.

target: इस मिठाई को गुलाब जामुन कहते हैं।
english: This sweet is called gulab jamun.
reason: आदर्श गाँव is a government-scheme label, not everyday talk. Same X को Y कहते हैं pattern on something a learner will actually name.

target: माली ने बाल्टी से पौधों को पानी दिया।
english: The gardener watered the plants with a bucket.
reason: "पानी वाला" sprinkling water is translationese for a role that is not a thing. Same ने + से-instrumental.

target: मैंने अलमारी में जगह बनाकर सामान रख दिया।
english: I made room in the cupboard and put the things away.
reason: Subjectless and built on niche vocabulary (ताक = wall niche). Same -कर participle with a subject and everyday objects.

target: हमारी दादी ने हमें बचपन में बहुत कहानियाँ सुनाईं।
english: Our grandmother told us lots of stories when we were little.
reason: Moralising motto ("taught us the lesson of love and respect"). Same ने + object + perfective, concrete memory instead.

target: यहाँ आजकल एक नया मकान बनाया जा रहा है।
english: A new house is being built here these days.
reason: Government-report officialese. Same progressive passive (…जा रहा है) in everyday speech.

target: खाने की खुशबू पूरे घर में फैल गई।
english: The smell of food spread through the whole house.
reason: Literary register — people say खाने की खुशबू, not खाना पकने की सुगंध. Same compound verb फैल गई.

target: ढोलक बजाने वाले ने शादी में गाना भी गाया।
english: The dholak player also sang a song at the wedding.
reason: Convoluted stacked participles (थाप देकर … बजाने वाले ने) with niche vocabulary. Same वाला agent noun, cleaner clause.

target: लोग धूप में कपड़े सुखाकर अलमारी में रखते हैं।
english: People dry the clothes in the sun and put them in the cupboard.
reason: Rural trivia (cow-dung fuel cakes) a learner will never use. Same generic लोग + -कर participle + habitual.

target: मेले में हज़ारों लोग घूमने आते हैं।
english: Thousands of people come to the fair to look around.
reason: Cultural trivia in formal register (श्रद्धालु, स्नान करना). Same large-number habitual statement, ordinary words.

target: रजिस्टर में सभी मेहमानों के नाम दर्ज हैं।
english: All the guests' names are recorded in the register.
reason: Academic officialese (bibliography, references). Same दर्ज हैं construction in a situation a learner meets.

target: चाय पीने से मुझे रात को नींद नहीं आती।
english: Drinking tea keeps me from sleeping at night.
reason: Textbook motto about the benefits of reading. Same verb-ने से causal structure, everyday observation.

target: इतनी तेज़ आवाज़ में बात करना ठीक नहीं है।
english: Talking that loudly isn't okay.
reason: Preachy etiquette maxim with literary कर्कश. Same infinitive-as-subject + adjective, plain wording.

target: ठंड में हम हीटर चलाकर बैठे रहे।
english: In the cold we sat with the heater on.
reason: Subjectless and stilted; the English gloss invents a subject that isn't there. Same -कर participle, subject restored.

target: मेज़ पर कागज़ों का ढेर लगा था।
english: There was a pile of papers on the table.
reason: Niche rural setting (खलिहान) plus the uncommon form ढेरी. Same ढेर लगा था existential past, everyday scene.
